title: Fast and accurate protein structure search with Foldseek

nodes.text: Foldseek aligns protein structures by describing tertiary amino acid interactions as sequences over a structural alphabet, reducing structure comparison to fast sequence alignment.
nodes.evidence: Foldseek aligns the structure of a query protein against a database by describing tertiary amino acid interactions within proteins as sequences over a structural alphabet.

nodes.text: The 3Di structural alphabet has 20 states, each describing the geometric conformation of a residue i with its spatially closest residue j, learned via a VQ-VAE modified to produce maximally evolutionarily conserved states.
nodes.evidence: The 20 states of the 3D interaction (3Di) alphabet describe for each residue i the geometric conformation with its spatially closest residue j ... by training a VQ-VAE28 modified to learn states that are maximally evolutionary conserved.

nodes.text: Unlike traditional backbone structural alphabets (CLE, 3D-BLAST, Protein Blocks) that discretize short Calpha stretches, 3Di describes tertiary interactions, giving weaker dependency between consecutive letters, more evenly distributed state frequencies, and highest information density in conserved cores.
nodes.evidence: 3Di has three key advantages over traditional backbone structural alphabets. (1) Weaker dependency between consecutive letters and (2) more evenly distributed state frequencies ... (3) The highest information density is encoded in conserved protein cores

nodes.text: Foldseek reuses the k-mer-based double-diagonal and gapless alignment prefilters from MMseqs2 on 3Di sequences, then performs vectorized Smith-Waterman local alignment combining 3Di and amino acid substitution scores, or optionally an accelerated TM-align global alignment.
nodes.evidence: we apply the fast and sensitive k-mer and ungapped alignment prefilter of MMseqs2 to the 3Di sequences, (2) followed by vectorized Smith-Waterman local alignment combining 3Di and amino acid substitution scores.

nodes.text: Foldseek decreases computation times by four to five orders of magnitude while reaching 86%, 88%, and 133% of the sensitivities of Dali, TM-align, and CE respectively.
nodes.evidence: Foldseek decreases computation times by four to five orders of magnitude with 86%, 88% and 133% of the sensitivities of Dali, TM-align and CE, respectively.

nodes.text: On the SCOPe40 benchmark Foldseek is more than 4,000 times faster than TM-align and Dali and over 21,000 times faster than CE; on AlphaFoldDB v1 it is around 184,600 and 23,000 times faster than Dali and TM-align.
nodes.evidence: Foldseek is more than 4,000 times faster than TM-align and Dali and over 21,000 times faster than CE ... around 184,600 and 23,000 times faster than Dali and TM-align

nodes.text: Foldseek-TM improves over TM-align in precision-recall because its prefilter suppresses high-scoring false positives.
nodes.evidence: Foldseek-TM improves over TM-align because its prefilter suppresses high-scoring FPs.

nodes.text: Like the 2D aligner Dali but unlike 3D aligners such as TM-align, Foldseek is independent of relative domain orientations and excels at detecting homologous multi-domain structures that are not globally superposable.
nodes.evidence: 3D aligners such as TM-align may overlook homologous structures that are not globally superposable, whereas Foldseek (as well as the two-dimensional (2D) aligner Dali) is independent of relative domain orientations

nodes.text: Foldseek alignments are more accurate and sensitive than MMseqs2, CLE-SW, and TM-align, similarly accurate as Dali, and 13% less precise but 15% more sensitive than CE.
nodes.evidence: Foldseek alignments are more accurate and sensitive than MMseqs2, CLE-SW and TM-align, similarly accurate as Dali and 13% less precise but 15% more sensitive than CE.

nodes.text: Foldseek improves E-value reliability by subtracting the reversed-query alignment score, applying a local compositional bias correction, and predicting extreme-value distribution parameters with a neural network based on 3Di composition and query length.
nodes.evidence: we subtracted the reversed query alignment score from the original score and applied a compositional bias correction ... parameters predicted by a neural network based on 3Di sequence composition and query length

nodes.text: On a SARS-CoV-2 RdRp query against AlphaFoldDB v1, Foldseek took 6 seconds versus 33 hours for TM-align and 10 days for Dali, with all top 10 hits being known RdRp homologs.
nodes.evidence: Search times were 10 d for Dali, 33 h for TM-align and 6 s for Foldseek ... All top 10 hits were known RdRp homologs

nodes.text: Because high-quality predicted structures are now available for nearly every folded protein, sequence-based analyses will soon be largely superseded by structure-based analyses once the speed bottleneck is removed.
nodes.evidence: Sequence-based analyses will soon be largely superseded by structure-based analyses.
